subject.title: fix embedded compaction hook reset API

question: Should `after_compaction` hook contexts gain the permanent public API `ctx.api.resetSession(reason?)`, with reset authority limited to the current canonical session and drained by the owning lifecycle?
rationale: This is a new compatibility-sensitive plugin contract and policy capability; source correctness cannot determine whether maintainers want session-reset authority exposed through hook context or retained behind an owner-specific internal boundary.

options.title: Approve the narrow hook API
options.body: Sponsor the after-compaction-only contract, require the unrelated changes to be split out, document its deferred semantics, and require positive live reset proof before merge.

options.title: Keep reset policy internal
options.body: Remove the public hook API and expose only an owner-specific internal lifecycle mechanism until a broader plugin session-control design is approved.

options.title: Pause this direction
options.body: Leave current reset commands and Gateway APIs unchanged and close or substantially redesign this PR if hook-triggered session rotation is not a desired core capability.

recommendation.title: Approve the narrow hook API
recommendation.body: Sponsor the after-compaction-only contract, require the unrelated changes to be split out, document its deferred semantics, and require positive live reset proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest feature-history signal covers both the plugin hook context and Codex hook integration affected by this decision.
